title: Complete and incomplete metamorphosis in insects
examples: What is the difference between complete and incomplete metamorphosis?

explain.say: Most insects change shape as they grow up, which is called metamorphosis. There are two main kinds: complete, with four stages, and incomplete, with three.

draw.text: Complete and incomplete metamorphosis in insects

explain.say: Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: the life cycle of a butterfly. Look at the eggs, the caterpillar and the chrysalis. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

draw.text: Complete and incomplete metamorphosis in insects

explain.say: In complete metamorphosis the larva, such as a caterpillar or maggot, is an eating machine that sheds its skin several times as it grows. It looks nothing like the adult and often eats different food, so young and adults don't compete.

stages.note: Laid on the right food plant

stages.label: Larva
stages.note: Eats and grows, moulting its skin

explain.say: Inside the pupa, much of the larva's body is broken down. Groups of cells called imaginal discs, carried since the egg, grow into the adult's wings, legs, eyes and antennae.

stages.label: Egg
stages.note: Laid on the right food plant

stages.label: Larva
stages.note: Eats and grows, moulting its skin

explain.say: In incomplete metamorphosis there is no pupa. A young grasshopper, called a nymph, looks like a small wingless adult and grows wing buds that get bigger with each moult.

faq.a: Inside the pupa, much of the larva's body is broken down into a soup of cells. Small groups of cells called imaginal discs, there since the egg, grow into the adult's wings, legs, eyes and antennae.
asks: How does a caterpillar turn into a butterfly?

faq.q: What is the difference between complete and incomplete metamorphosis?
faq.a: Complete metamorphosis has four stages, egg, larva, pupa and adult, and the young look nothing like the adults. Incomplete metamorphosis has three, egg, nymph and adult, and the young look like small adults without wings.
asks: Which insects have a pupa stage?

faq.a: A nymph is the young stage of an insect with incomplete metamorphosis, like a grasshopper or cockroach. It resembles a small adult without working wings and moults several times as it grows.
asks: What is a baby grasshopper called?

faq.q: What controls when an insect moults?
faq.a: Hormones. A moulting hormone called ecdysone triggers each moult, and juvenile hormone decides what comes out: while it is high the insect stays young, and when it falls the insect becomes a pupa or adult.
asks: Why does an insect shed its skin?

faq.q: Why do insects go through metamorphosis?
faq.a: Splitting life into stages lets larvae and adults use different food and homes, so they do not compete. The larva specialises in eating and growing, and the adult in spreading and breeding.
asks: What is the point of metamorphosis?
Why don't baby insects look like adults?

facts: Beetles, butterflies, moths, flies, bees, wasps and ants all go through complete metamorphosis.
Two hormones control moulting: ecdysone triggers each moult, and juvenile hormone keeps the insect in its young form.

quiz.why: Caterpillars eat leaves and butterflies sip nectar, so the two stages never fight over the same food.
